title: TCE-MG's Alice audit of 2,297 August 2022 tenders detects 60 irregularities worth R$113.7 million; 53 alerts answered and notices worth R$91.7 million corrected
summary: TCE-MG audit with Alice of 2,297 Aug 2022 tenders: 60 irregularities (R$113,713,128.26); 53 alerts answered; notices corrected worth R$91,723,011.31 (TCE-MG, 27 June 2023).
account: The Tribunal de Contas do Estado de Minas Gerais (TCE-MG) is one of more than ten Brazilian courts of accounts that adopted Alice. Alice is the Análise de Licitações e Editais system created by the CGU and the TCU. In December 2022 it published an audit of 2,297 municipal and state tenders held in a single month, August 2022. The exact day is not given. The court's own news item of 27 June 2023, reproduced by Atricon on 28 June 2023, gives the results. The work detected 60 irregularities involving R$113,713,128.26. 53 of the 60 alerts sent to the audited bodies received answers that allowed control verification. Irregularities were fixed in republished notices or measures adopted for future tenders. The audit achieved corrected notices worth R$91,723,011.31. The figures are aggregates presented by analysts Maria Aparecida Aiko Ikemura and Leonardo Alves Mateus to about 60 people from courts of accounts across Brazil. No individual tender is named.
purpose: Automated identification of tender notices with possible inconsistencies or irregularities so that the court can oversee more tenders. This use was its intended purpose.
system: Alice (Análise de Licitações e Editais), the CGU/TCU tender-analysis system as adopted by TCE-MG
developer: Controladoria-Geral da União (CGU) and Tribunal de Contas da União (TCU)
deployer: Tribunal de Contas do Estado de Minas Gerais (TCE-MG)
domain: Public administration: state external audit and procurement control
segment: State court of accounts (anti-waste and anti-corruption control)
taxonomy_note: The value corrected is that of the notices, not money saved.

ratings.reason: No individual beneficiary is identified. Beneficiaries are public bodies and bidders in corrected tenders.
Material to the audited municipal and state bodies: 53 of 60 alerts answered and notices worth R$91,723,011.31 corrected, per the court's own aggregate figures.
One month of tenders in one state. The statement gives no estimate of money saved, only the value of notices corrected.

ai_role.statement: Alice produced the alerts on the 2,297 tenders. TCE-MG analysts forwarded 60 alerts and the audited bodies made the corrections. The AI role was detection and triage. The only sources are the deployer's own news item (TCE-MG, 27 June 2023) and Atricon's reproduction of it the next day. No audit report, tender or court decision is among the sources. TCE-MG did not build the tool (CGU/TCU did), so the statement is not vendor-authored. It is the user describing its own results.

Selection of a typology of irregularities and a designed oversight process
Alerts sent to the audited bodies with a request for response
Audited bodies republishing corrected notices or adopting measures for future tenders
must_hold: Access to state and municipal tender notices in machine-readable form

Audited bodies answering alerts (53 of 60 did)

TCE-MG presented Alice and Solaris to TCE-ES (Espírito Santo) for adoption; no outcome reported

headline: Alice audit at TCE-MG corrects notices worth R$91.7 million
metric: the audit achieved corrections of notices worth R$91,723,011.31

later.note: In January 2024 TCE-MG was still running Alice and presented its methodology and results to a TCE-ES auditor who had asked to learn about the robots; adoption by TCE-ES is not reported.
later.quote: Conhecer a metodologia e resultados do TCEMG com a utilização dos robôs Solaris e Alice, bem como as ações implementadas pela Corte de Contas mineira com os dados e informações obtidos com as fiscalizações feitas pelos robôs. Com esses objetivos, o auditor Bruno Fardin Faé, do Tribunal de Contas do Espírito Santos (TCE-ES), solicitou ao TCE-MG uma reunião virtual com a equipe do Suricato, que ocorreu na manhã desta quarta-feira (16).
